completion_conditions: After a full loop cycle including the closeout, `git merge origin/main` succeeds in the coordinator checkout with no manual step.
It still succeeds on a second cycle.
A newly added effector is covered without further change — staging happens at one point, not per-effector.
Nothing outside .shiki/ is staged and nothing is committed in the coordinator.
The full suite, the goal-loop suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: MEASURED, WITH THE FIX PRESENT. The coordinator carried the merged staging fix (`git add -- *copied` in `_sync_state_to_branch`) from 15:27; the fix reached main at 15:09. At 15:46, after the closeout loop completed, `git merge origin/main` still aborted with 'The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge', naming six records written at 15:46 — AFTER the fix was in place.

THE SIX: `.shiki/goals/G-...4f95b5bf.json`, `.shiki/locks/T-...52142739.json`, `.shiki/tasks/T-...52142739.json`, two closeout ledgers, and `.shiki/reports/R-...18fd8360.json`. Every one is a closeout-era write.

CAUSE, read from source. `_sync_state_to_branch` has exactly three call sites — `:2063` create_pr, `:2103` dispatch_repair, `:2167` rerun_cca — so the staging added to it reaches only those. The `merge`, `mark_done`, `goal_complete` and `create_closeout_pr` effectors write the coordinator mirror through their own paths and stage nothing. `_create_closeout_pr` (`:1500`) builds the terminal state in a FRESH worktree cut from origin/main and commits there; the coordinator's own copies of the same records are written separately and left untracked.

SCOPE OF THE PREVIOUS TASK WAS RIGHT, ITS COVERAGE WAS NOT. Its acceptance criterion was 'after a loop cycle that writes mirror records, git merge origin/main succeeds' — the criterion is correct and remains the target. The implementation satisfied the letter of its scope prose (which named `_sync_state_to_branch`) and not the criterion. The CCA returned `complete` after verifying the change matched the scope; it did not drive the criterion end to end. That gap is recorded here, not repaired here.

DESIGN. Do not scatter a `git add` into each effector: `execute_action` has eleven branches (`:1983`-`:2227`) and any new one would silently reintroduce the defect. Stage once, at a single point that covers every effector — the loop's own `.shiki` working surface in the coordinator — so a future effector is covered by construction. STAGING ONLY, never committing: the coordinator's local branch must not advance.

MUST NOT: delete or move any mirror record to avoid the collision (the mirror is append-only evidence); stage anything outside `.shiki/`; change `_sync_state_to_branch`'s signature (`tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py:209-224` monkeypatches it) or what `_evidence_relatives_for_task` returns (`tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py` asserts on it at `:320`, `:336`, `:498`); change what the closeout PR contains or the decision table `docs/adr/0012` pins.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-06). MUST-CHANGE: `scripts/shiki_loop.py`; `tests/test_closeout.py` (47 references — owns the closeout effectors, where the six uncovered records are written); `tests/test_dispatch_state_sync.py` (owns the staging property the previous task introduced, and its assertion must widen from the sync paths to every effector).

MUST-NOT-BREAK (verification command, not locks): `tests/test_loop_branch_plumbing.py`, `tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py`, `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py`, `tests/test_loop_engine.py`, and `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh`, which drives the loop end to end including the closeout.

Risk is medium: this changes only which paths the loop stages in its own coordinator checkout. No gate, schema, workflow, approval source or delivered artifact moves. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) neither PR triggers the Guardian gate.

amendments: 2026-08-06 SCOPE AMENDMENT, from measuring the merged implementation against this task's own acceptance criterion. The criterion is still false, and the cause is a constraint I placed in the contract WITHOUT measuring it. (1) MEASURED IN A MINIMAL REPRO. Staging alone does not clear the merge. With the colliding path STAGED and byte-identical to the incoming version: a FAST-FORWARD merge succeeds, but a NON-fast-forward merge fails with 'error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge'. The coordinator always carries its own commits, so it is always the non-fast-forward case. `git add` therefore only renamed the failure - 'untracked would be overwritten' became 'local changes would be overwritten' - and the manual back-up-and-delete is still required. (2) COMMITTING DOES CLEAR IT, measured in the same repro: non-fast-forward, committed, byte-identical -> 'Merge made by the ort strategy', clean, zero manual steps. Today's real collisions were 27 of 28 and 20 of 20 byte-identical, so committing resolves the overwhelming majority automatically. (3) A GENUINE DIVERGENCE STILL CONFLICTS, and that is correct. Non-fast-forward, committed, DIFFERING content -> 'CONFLICT (add/add)'. That is a normal, resolvable merge conflict rather than a hard refusal, and it means the two sides really do disagree; main is the source of truth and wins. Eliminating it is explicitly NOT in scope - it must be documented, not suppressed. MY ERROR, recorded because it is the reusable lesson: the original contract's non-goal 'Committing in the coordinator - the local branch must not advance' was mine, asserted without measurement, and it is precisely what made the design unable to satisfy the criterion. The coordinator's branch is a disposable execution surface that is never merged anywhere (AGENTS.md: 'Worktrees are disposable execution surfaces'), so advancing it costs nothing. That non-goal is REMOVED. TEST CONTRACT CORRECTED. The previous tests passed while the criterion was false because their temporary repositories were not divergent, so they only ever exercised the fast-forward path. Every merge assertion must now build a repository whose coordinator branch carries its own commit, making the merge NON-fast-forward - the case that actually occurs.

tasks.scope:
Make the loop's coordinator-side mirror writes survive a later `git merge origin/main` without a manual step. The previous implementation staged them; measurement shows staging is not enough.

MEASURED IN A MINIMAL REPRO, with the colliding path byte-identical to the incoming version:
  staged + FAST-FORWARD merge          -> succeeds
  staged + NON-fast-forward merge      -> 'error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge'
  committed + NON-fast-forward merge   -> 'Merge made by the ort strategy', clean
The coordinator always carries its own commits, so it is ALWAYS the non-fast-forward case. `git add` only renamed the failure.

COMMIT the coordinator's `.shiki` writes, do not merely stage them. Keep every other property the previous implementation established: one covering point that every effector in `execute_action` passes through (eleven branches, `:1983`-`:2227`) so a future effector is covered by construction; scoped to `.shiki` so nothing outside the mirror is ever touched; and never staging a deletion, so the append-only mirror cannot be emptied by this path.

THE REMOVED CONSTRAINT. The previous contract's non-goal 'Committing in the coordinator — the local branch must not advance' was asserted without measurement and is exactly what made the design unable to satisfy its own criterion. It is REMOVED. The coordinator's branch is a disposable execution surface that is never merged anywhere, so advancing it costs nothing. Commit only the mirror; never commit anything outside `.shiki`.

WHAT REMAINS, AND MUST BE DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED: when the coordinator's copy and the incoming version genuinely DIFFER, the merge produces a normal `CONFLICT (add/add)` instead of a hard refusal. That is correct — the two sides really do disagree, and main is the source of truth. Do not add a merge driver, a strategy option, or any automatic resolution: state the behaviour in a comment and leave the resolution to the operator. Measured today: 27 of 28 and 20 of 20 real collisions were byte-identical, so this path is the exception, not the rule.

TEST CONTRACT, CORRECTED — this is why the previous implementation passed while its criterion was false. Its tests built temporary repositories that were NOT divergent, so they only ever exercised the fast-forward path. EVERY merge assertion must now build a repository whose coordinator branch carries its own commit, so the merge is NON-fast-forward. Assert: after a full cycle including the closeout, the non-fast-forward merge succeeds with no manual step; it still succeeds on a second cycle; a genuinely differing file produces a normal conflict and NOT a refusal; nothing outside `.shiki` is committed; and no mirror record is deleted.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: `git merge origin/main` in the coordinator still aborts after a loop cycle, now with 'Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge' instead of the untracked variant.
  Measured in a minimal repro (three repositories, identical content, fast-forward vs divergent): staging clears only the fast-forward case; committing clears the divergent case too.
  Root cause: a non-goal in the previous contract — 'the local branch must not advance' — asserted without measurement.
  Reproducible when: a divergent coordinator merges origin/main with no manual step, twice in a row, and a genuinely differing file yields a conflict rather than a refusal.
